supermarket.note: Shrimp, squid, and clams. Pre-cleaned, ready to use straight from the bag.

tools.name: Frying pan with a lid (about 24 cm)
tools.note: The pan stands in for a pot. No lid? An upturned plate works too.

tools.name: Measuring cup
tools.note: A mug is fine. A typical mug holds about 250 ml.

tools.name: Peeler
tools.note: Carrot skin is edible. Wash well and you can skip peeling.

steps.title: Cut carrots
points: Cut the carrots into thin quarter-rounds, about 3 mm thick.
Two small carrots are about a handful of slices.
steps.hint: A frying pan holds less water than a pot, so thin slices are the trick to cooking everything through before the liquid reduces away.

steps.title: Slice onion
points: Keep it about as fine as the carrots so both cook in the same time.

steps.title: Fry vegetables
points: Melt 1 tbsp of butter over medium heat.
Add the carrots and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the onion and cook 3 minutes more, until translucent.
steps.hint: Don't turn the heat up high. Butter burns at high temperatures and turns bitter.

steps.title: Simmer vegetables
points: Add 250 ml of water and bring it to a boil.
Drop the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes.
steps.hint: Poke a carrot with the tip of a knife to check. If it slides in without resistance, it's done.

steps.title: Add roux
points: Break in the 2 blocks and stir until completely dissolved.
steps.hint: Turning off the heat matters. Roux added to boiling liquid goes lumpy, and it scorches in a thin pan.

steps.title: Add seafood
points: Add the seafood straight from frozen.
Return to low heat and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring gently.
steps.hint: When the shrimp turn opaque and the squid curls up, it's cooked. Any longer and the squid turns rubbery.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Turn it out onto a plate and fluff it with a spoon.

steps.title: Serve curry
points: Stir the last of the butter through the pan off the heat.
Ladle the curry beside the rice rather than on top.

troubleshooting.solution: The frozen seafood released water. Take the seafood out, simmer uncovered for 2 minutes to reduce, then return it.
With the heat off, add water 2 tablespoons at a time, stirring after each addition.
Press it against the side of the pan with a spoon. It's pressure that breaks it down, not heat.
It was simmered too long. Next time, start a 4-minute timer the moment the seafood goes in.
